Classification guard: case-matching edge following the batch-30 episcleritis and erythromelalgia unexplained-chronic-pain precedent - the documented neuropathic pain feature of femoral neuropathy is mapped as a pain-burden association only, with the target's own criteria requiring competing pain generators excluded at the individual level; individual claims require documented femoral mononeuropathy with electrodiagnostic confirmation, documented pain distribution, and exclusion of lumbar, vascular, hip, and centralized pain generators.
governanceNotes: D1 batch 34 (2026-09-23): one bounded unexplained-chronic-pain association authored under the batch-30 pain-constitutive case-matching precedent - the Santilli 2024 Mayo Clinic clinical and electrodiagnostic review of 159 isolated femoral neuropathy patients documents pain as a presenting feature in 53% alongside weakness in 96% with only 48% achieving nearly complete recovery at follow-up, the Martinoli 2013 Eur J Radiol review documents that neuropathies about the hip (including the femoral nerve) may be a cause of chronic pain and disability, and the Malik 2023 case documents severe neuropathic pain with femoral nerve palsy after cardiac intervention; the pain feature is constitutive/presenting rather than a proven downstream outcome, so the edge serves case-matching only exactly as the batch-30 pain edges do.

Negative screens recorded 2026-09-23: (i) falls and knee-injury outcomes - the targeted femoral-neuropathy-with-falls search returned only three records (a five-patient knee-immobilizer series by Jones 2004 with falls as an outcome measure, the Kromoser 2025 synovial-cyst recurrent-falls case, and the Lyme femoral-mononeuropathy case), all case-level with no cohort quantification, and no falls identity exists in the catalog; (ii) knee-instability outcomes - the 23 knee hits are dominated by knee-extension-deficit descriptions (the deficit itself) and etiology papers, with no knee-injury outcome cohort. Duplicate-scope note: the unexplained-chronic-pain target carries two batch-30 edges (episcleritis, erythromelalgia) on small-fiber mechanisms; this edge adds the large-fiber mononeuropathic pain mechanism with an independent evidence base.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The Santilli 2024 Mayo Clinic review of 159 isolated femoral neuropathy patients documents pain as a presenting feature in 53% with weakness in 96% and only 48% achieving nearly complete recovery over a mean 14.8-month recovery course, the Martinoli 2013 review documents that neuropathies about the hip may be a cause of chronic pain and disability, and the Malik 2023 case documents severe neuropathic pain with femoral nerve palsy; the literature documents the pain feature of the identity without establishing that femoral neuropathy produces a primary chronic-pain syndrome in an individual.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: The mapping does not assert that femoral neuropathy causes the target's unexplained-pain state: pain is a presenting feature rather than a demonstrated downstream outcome, the documented nerve lesion is itself a pain generator that the target's own criteria treat as a competing generator to characterize carefully, and lumbar radiculopathy, vascular claudication, hip osteoarthritis, complex regional pain syndrome, and centralized pain all mimic or accompany femoral-distribution pain; individual claims require electrodiagnostically documented femoral mononeuropathy, documented pain distribution and chronology, and exclusion of the competing generators per the target's criteria.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized peripheral-nerve-injury central-sensitization pathway: femoral-nerve compression, stretch, or inflammatory injury generates persistent nociceptive input from the anterior thigh and knee region; sustained input can centralize in dorsal-horn and supraspinal pain-processing circuits, lowering pain thresholds and extending pain beyond the acute injury window - consistent with the Santilli finding that improvement is often prolonged and incomplete; the pathway remains a hypothesis about an individual's course because most cohorts describe pain at presentation without characterizing chronic-pain evolution.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is a case-matching association only: the pain evidence is a presenting-symptom share from a single-center retrospective review plus case-level reports, no femoral-neuropathy cohort quantifies chronic-pain incidence or chronic-pain-syndrome evolution, the identity's defining deficit is weakness (96%) rather than pain, and competing generators are common in the same distributions; no probability estimate is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Electrodiagnostic or clinical documentation of femoral mononeuropathy with etiology (compressive, perioperative stretch, inflammatory); pain documentation with distribution, severity scale, and chronology relative to the neuropathy; persistence of pain beyond the expected recovery course if chronic pain is claimed; exclusion of lumbar radiculopathy, peripheral arterial disease, hip osteoarthritis, complex regional pain syndrome, and centralized pain; neurology and pain-medicine assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Peripheral arterial disease with claudication or critical ischemia
Hip osteoarthritis or other intra-articular hip pathology
Fibromyalgia or centralized pain of independent origin
